title: Effect of photocatalytic pretreatment on the biodegradation of n-hexane vapours in a biofilter
author: Hajizadeh, Jafari, et al.
materials: All chemicals for preparation of the nutrient solution and TiO2 nano-powder (TiO2, anatase, ≥99%) were prepared from Merck Company. TiO2 coating was performed according to the follow procedures:(1)10 g of TiO2 powder was added to 150 mL of ethanol and its pH was adjusted at 3.5 HNO3 (0.5 N).(2)The resulting slurry was entirely diffused with an ultrasound bath (15 min).(3)For coating, the TiO2 on the scoria granules, 45 g of these granules were shed to the slurry and slowly blended for 1 h to provide better adsorption of the TiO2 onto the granules.(4)The slurry solution was evaporated at 80 °C.(5)The scoria granules were calcinated at 450 °C in a laboratory furnace for 30 min.

Finally, for removing the catalyst which is not attached properly to the scoria granules, the granules washed 2 times with distilled water and air bubbling for a few minutes. More details are available in our previous study [11].

steps.title: Prepare TiO2‑coated scoria granules
steps.instruction: Coat scoria granules with TiO2 following the sequence below.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 g TiO₂ (anatase, ≥99 %) to 150 mL ethanol and adjust the pH to 3.5 using 0.5 N HNO₃.
Ultrasonicate the resulting slurry in an ultrasound bath for 15 min.
Add 45 g scoria granules to the slurry and blend slowly for 1 h to promote TiO₂ adsorption onto the granules.
Evaporate the slurry by heating to 80 °C until the solvent is removed.
Calcine the dried, TiO₂‑coated granules in a laboratory furnace at 450 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Wash coated granules
steps.instruction: Remove loosely attached TiO₂ by rinsing the granules twice with distilled water and bubbling air through the suspension for a few minutes.

steps.title: Collect gas samples for analysis
steps.instruction: Sample inlet and outlet gas streams using a gas‑tight syringe and prepare them for GC‑FID measurement.

substeps.instruction: Withdraw 0.5 mL of inlet‑stream polluted gas with a gas‑tight syringe.
Withdraw 0.5 mL of outlet‑stream gas with the same syringe.
Inject each 0.5 mL sample directly into the GC‑FID (Varian CP‑3800, USA) equipped with an FID detector.

steps.title: Analyze samples and calculate removal efficiency
steps.instruction: Run the GC‑FID analysis, record concentrations, and compute removal efficiency using the collected data.

substeps.instruction: Take more than 1000 samples over the operation period, collecting two samples per day from each sampling point.
Average the duplicate daily measurements and express the results in g · m⁻³.
Calculate the removal efficiency (RE) of n‑hexane from inlet and outlet concentrations.
